Cystitis: suprapubic tenderness, bacteriuria; urethritis → **distal anterior vaginal wall tenderness**, sterile pyuria

congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia.core: Newborn salt loss or atypical genitalia demands adrenal evaluation; hypertension with abnormal puberty suggests a different steroid-synthesis block.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive inheritance; affected sibling, consanguinity
Classic disease presents neonatally; partial enzyme deficiency may present with adolescent androgen excess

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Neonatal vomiting, weight loss, dehydration, **shock**, ↓Na, ↓glucose → salt-wasting adrenal crisis
46,XX virilization with internal female organs; 46,XY infants may lack obvious external warning signs
Nonclassic 21-hydroxylase deficiency: premature pubarche, hirsutism, acne or irregular menses

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Low cortisol removes feedback → ↑ACTH and adrenal hyperplasia
Steroid precursors accumulate upstream; androgen and mineralocorticoid effects depend on enzyme block

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **17-hydroxyprogesterone** screens for 21-hydroxylase deficiency; elevated values → confirmatory steroid testing
Borderline nonclassic disease → ACTH-stimulated 17-OHP; electrolytes, renin, cortisol and androgens guide subtype
Ambiguous genitalia → karyotype, pelvic ultrasound, endocrine consultation; avoid premature sex assignment
Newborn screen may miss milder disease; clinical instability overrides screening results

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crisis → **IV hydrocortisone**, isotonic saline, dextrose; treat severe hyperkalemia
Glucocorticoid replacement suppresses ACTH; salt-wasting forms → fludrocortisone plus infant salt supplementation
11β/17α-associated hypertension → glucocorticoids; add antihypertensives for persistent elevation
Genital differences → multidisciplinary counseling; timing of surgery requires informed shared decisions

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated crisis → death; androgen excess → precocious pseudopuberty, advanced bone age, short adult height
Excess replacement → growth suppression, obesity, osteoporosis; inadequate replacement → infertility/adrenal rest tumors

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Newborn screening, genetic counseling; emergency steroid kit, medical alert, illness/surgery stress dosing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Androgen insensitivity: 46,XY, testes, absent uterus, normal adrenal steroids
Pyloric stenosis: vomiting with hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis rather than salt-wasting hyperkalemia

congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

congenital-infections.name: Congenital infections
congenital-infections.scope: Cytomegalovirus (sensorineural hearing loss, periventricular calcifications), Toxoplasmosis (chorioretinitis), Parvovirus B19 (hydrops), Rubella, Varicella, Zika, screening and diagnosis
congenital-infections.core: Congenital infection causes growth restriction, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, or hydrops; organ-specific patterns identify the pathogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CMV: toddler saliva/urine; toxoplasma: undercooked meat, cat feces; B19: child with slapped-cheek rash
Absent rubella/varicella immunity; mosquito exposure or sexual transmission in Zika-risk areas

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae/blueberry-muffin lesions, abnormal fetal ultrasound; many infected newborns initially appear well
★ B19 hydrops: cardiomegaly, ascites, edema without red-cell alloantibodies
Maternal rash: B19 → slapped cheek, then reticular limb rash; rubella → descending rash, postauricular nodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transplacental infection disrupts organogenesis; later exposure may cause inflammation or marrow suppression
Toxoplasma transmission increases with gestational age; earlier infection causes more severe injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal exposure → pathogen-specific **IgG/IgM**, paired titers or avidity; isolated IgM needs confirmation
★ CMV newborn diagnosis: saliva PCR then confirm urine PCR **within 21 days**
Suspected fetal infection → targeted ultrasound, pathogen-specific amniotic-fluid PCR; B19 → serial MCA Doppler
Prenatal rubella IgG routinely; no universal US maternal CMV, toxoplasma, or B19 screening

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic congenital CMV → **valganciclovir**, monitor CBC and liver tests
Congenital toxoplasmosis → pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin; maternal regimen depends on fetal infection
B19 severe fetal anemia → intrauterine transfusion; rubella/Zika structural injury → supportive care
Maternal varicella exposure without immunity → varicella-zoster immune globulin; maternal pneumonia → IV acyclovir
Maternal varicella onset 5 days before to 2 days after delivery → **newborn VZIG**

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, neurodevelopmental disability; delayed/progressive hearing loss requires longitudinal audiology

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Rubella/varicella vaccination before pregnancy or postpartum; **live vaccines contraindicated during pregnancy**
Handwashing after diapers; cook meat, avoid litter handling; mosquito precautions and Zika exposure counseling
Term newborn of varicella-immune mother: transplacental IgG protects → no prophylaxis after exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aneuploidy: abnormal genetic testing rather than pathogen testing
Rh disease: positive maternal antibody screen with fetal anemia

table.title: Discriminating congenital patterns
rows: Periventricular calcifications, microcephaly, sensorineural hearing loss, chorioretinitis
Severe microcephaly, subcortical calcifications, ocular abnormalities

congenital-infections.evidence: CMV testing checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/cytomegalovirus/hcp/clinical-overview/index.html); remaining pathogen patterns established teaching.

contraception.name: Contraception
contraception.scope: Combined oral contraceptives, progestin-only pills, implant, intrauterine devices, tubal sterilization
contraception.core: Choose contraception through shared decisions about efficacy, bleeding, reversibility, adherence, and estrogen-related vascular risk.

rows.label: Who
items: Anyone seeking pregnancy prevention; adolescents and nulliparous patients can use IUDs or implants
Healthy patient: blood pressure suffices; **no pelvic exam** needed before oral contraceptives

rows.label: Schedule
items: Pills daily; depot medroxyprogesterone every 3 months; implants/IUDs last years (product-dependent)
★ Emergency contraception ≤**5 days**: copper IUD/ulipristal; levonorgestrel ≤72 h, no medical contraindications
Progestin-only pills: daily timing crucial; norethindrone less forgiving than drospirenone

rows.label: Special groups
items: Breastfeeding (estrogen lowers milk volume, protein) or estrogen contraindication → progestin-only or copper IUD
Current breast cancer → copper IUD; avoid hormonal methods
Prior VTE, poor adherence → **IUD/implant** (depot raises VTE risk); older exams: depot, avoid IUD after STI

rows.label: Choice
items: Combined pills: suppress ovulation, improve acne/cramps, reduce endometrial/ovarian cancer risk
★ **LARC** minimizes adherence failures; condoms add STI protection
Tubal sterilization: permanent; counsel regret, alternatives, surgical risk, ectopic risk after failure

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Estrogen: **migraine with aura, prior VTE/thrombophilia**, hypertension (stop pill), early postpartum
Smoking age ≥35: combined methods usually avoid; ≥15 cigarettes/day → absolute contraindication
IUD: pregnancy, cervicitis/PID, distorted cavity (non-distorting fibroid OK); copper: also Wilson disease

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Same-day STI screening need not delay insertion without cervicitis; prior PID alone permits IUD
Sterilization: voluntary informed consent; no required partner approval, parity, or marital status
After ulipristal, wait 5 days before progestin; backup contraception needed after hormonal restart

table.title: Long-acting choices
rows: Treats heavy menses; atrophy → expected benign amenorrhea

dysmenorrhea.name: Dysmenorrhea
dysmenorrhea.scope: Primary dysmenorrhea, secondary dysmenorrhea (endometriosis, adenomyosis, cervical stenosis), hematometra, NSAIDs, combined oral contraceptives
dysmenorrhea.core: Painful menstruation: primary disease begins after ovulatory cycles develop; later-onset, progressive, or refractory pain suggests pelvic pathology.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Early menarche, heavy/prolonged flow, family history, smoking
Prior cervical excision/ablation → stenosis; endometriosis and adenomyosis produce secondary symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Suprapubic cramping radiating to back/thighs, nausea, diarrhea, headache
★ **Dyspareunia, abnormal bleeding, infertility**, or pain outside menses → secondary cause
Amenorrhea or scant flow after cervical procedure with cyclic pain → retained menstrual blood

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Progesterone withdrawal → endometrial prostaglandins → uterine hypercontractility and ischemia
Outflow obstruction traps blood in uterine cavity → hematometra

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Classic adolescent presentation without red flags → **clinical diagnosis**, no initial imaging
Sexual activity → pregnancy test; infection risks → gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Secondary features → pelvic examination and **transvaginal ultrasound**; transabdominal imaging if needed
No improvement after 3–6 months despite adherence → investigate secondary disease, consider laparoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NSAIDs**, starting 1–2 days before expected bleeding through first 2–3 days
★ Inadequate response/contraception desired → **combined OCP** or progestin; continuous suppression may help
Heat, exercise; avoid NSAIDs with active ulcer disease or significant renal dysfunction
Treat underlying lesion; cervical stenosis with hematometra → cervical dilation/drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: School/work absence, sleep disturbance; untreated secondary disease may impair fertility
Analgesic adverse effects: GI bleeding, renal injury; estrogen-containing contraception → VTE risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Track cycles and preempt pain; ongoing menstrual suppression reduces recurrence when pregnancy not desired

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, nonmenstrual bleeding, possible instability
PID: fever, mucopurulent discharge, cervical motion tenderness

table.title: Secondary patterns
rows: Posterior nodularity; ultrasound may be normal
Heavy bleeding, boggy uniformly enlarged uterus

dysmenorrhea.evidence: Not checked online; established adolescent gynecology and pelvic-pain teaching.

early-pregnancy-loss.name: Early pregnancy loss
early-pregnancy-loss.scope: Threatened abortion, inevitable abortion, incomplete abortion, complete abortion, missed abortion, anembryonic pregnancy
early-pregnancy-loss.core: First-trimester bleeding requires pregnancy location and viability assessment before labeling miscarriage or choosing expectant, medical, or surgical management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Embryonic aneuploidy most common; maternal age, prior losses, uterine anomalies, antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Clues
items: Cramping, vaginal bleeding, passage of tissue; symptoms may be absent with retained nonviable pregnancy
★ Hypotension, syncope, peritoneal signs → **hemorrhage or ruptured ectopic**
Fever, uterine tenderness, foul discharge → septic abortion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryonic/fetal demise or failed embryonic development → decidual separation and variable cervical dilation
Corpus luteum progesterone sustains pregnancy until ~10 weeks; removal earlier → **progesterone supplementation**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** plus quantitative β-hCG; CBC, blood type, pelvic examination
Definitive nonviability: CRL ≥7 mm without heartbeat or mean sac diameter ≥25 mm without embryo
Absent embryo/heartbeat on repeat: ≥11 days after yolk sac, ≥14 days after sac-only → nonviable
No intrauterine pregnancy → serial hCG/ultrasound; tissue passage alone cannot exclude ectopic

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable, infected, or uncontrolled hemorrhage → **urgent uterine aspiration**; sepsis → IV broad-spectrum antibiotics
Confirmed stable loss → patient choice: observation, mifepristone followed by misoprostol, or aspiration
Threatened loss → expectant follow-up; bed rest does not prevent miscarriage
Stable, unlocated pregnancy, falling hCG → serial hCG until negative; no methotrexate
★ Rh-negative loss **≥12 weeks → RhIg**; ACOG omits routine testing earlier; older exam questions may expect Rh typing

rows.label: Complications
items: Retained products, infection, hemorrhage; intrauterine adhesions after instrumentation; grief/depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking/alcohol avoidance, optimize diabetes; most isolated chromosomal losses unpreventable
Recurrent clinical losses → assess uterine anatomy, antiphospholipid antibodies and selected genetic causes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine implantation, adnexal mass/free fluid
Gestational trophoblastic disease: very high hCG, abnormal cystic intrauterine tissue
Subchorionic hematoma: bleeding without cramping; viable intrauterine pregnancy, perichorionic collection
Normal early pregnancy: spotting, 5-week sac, hCG ~1,000, simple corpus luteum cyst; embryo not yet expected

fetal-growth-restriction.name: Fetal growth restriction
fetal-growth-restriction.scope: Symmetric vs asymmetric FGR, uteroplacental insufficiency, chromosomal anomalies, congenital infections, umbilical artery Doppler surveillance, oligohydramnios
fetal-growth-restriction.core: Estimated fetal weight or abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile requires evaluation for placental dysfunction and fetal disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal hypertension, preeclampsia, renal/vascular disease, smoking, cocaine, malnutrition, prior affected pregnancy
Aneuploidy, structural anomalies, CMV; multiple gestation

rows.label: Clues
items: Fundal height lag >3 cm, decreased movement, oligohydramnios; sometimes abnormal maternal placental disease markers
★ **EFW <3rd percentile** indicates severe disease; normal-size parents do not establish constitutional smallness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental resistance reduces oxygen/nutrients; redistribution preserves cerebral over abdominal growth
Low fetal renal perfusion reduces urine production and fluid volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Ultrasound biometry using reliable dating → detailed anatomy; serial growth generally every 3–4 weeks
★ **Umbilical artery Doppler every 1–2 weeks**; absent (AEDV)/reversed (REDV) diastolic velocity → intensified surveillance
Weekly NST after viability; increase frequency with Doppler deterioration or maternal comorbidity
Early <32 weeks, unexplained or anomalous → offer amniocentesis/microarray; CMV PCR if amniocentesis chosen
Do not order indiscriminate TORCH panels without exposure or suggestive findings

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Reversed flow → **hospitalization**, corticosteroids, frequent cardiotocography, delivery planning
Anticipated preterm birth → betamethasone; magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection before 32 weeks
Nonreassuring testing/maternal deterioration → earlier delivery; absent/reversed flow may favor cesarean
Bed rest, sildenafil, and LMWH solely to treat/prevent FGR provide no established benefit

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, intrapartum intolerance, neonatal hypoglycemia, hypothermia, polycythemia; later metabolic/cardiovascular risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Tobacco/drug cessation, maternal disease control; low-dose aspirin when preeclampsia-risk criteria met

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates: early ultrasound establishes gestational age
Constitutionally small fetus: reassuring interval growth and normal Doppler without placental disease

table.title: Patterns and delivery in otherwise stable disease
rows: Often later placental insufficiency; patterns overlap

gestational-trophoblastic-disease.name: Gestational trophoblastic disease
gestational-trophoblastic-disease.scope: Complete hydatidiform mole, partial hydatidiform mole, choriocarcinoma, suction curettage, serial beta-hCG surveillance, contraception
gestational-trophoblastic-disease.core: Abnormal trophoblastic proliferation causes excessive hCG, bleeding, and vesicular placental tissue; persistent hCG after evacuation suggests gestational trophoblastic neoplasia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior molar pregnancy, extremes of reproductive age; choriocarcinoma can follow any pregnancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Vaginal bleeding, hyperemesis, uterus larger than dates, bilateral theca lutein cysts
★ **Preeclampsia before 20 weeks** or gestational thyrotoxicosis → suspect mole
Postpregnancy bleeding with cough/hemoptysis or neurologic symptoms → metastatic trophoblastic malignancy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal fertilization produces proliferative hydropic villi; high hCG stimulates thyroid and ovarian receptors
Choriocarcinoma lacks chorionic villi and spreads hematogenously, especially to lungs, vagina, brain

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantitative **β-hCG + pelvic ultrasound**; snowstorm/multicystic placental appearance may be absent early
Evacuated tissue histopathology confirms; p57 absent in complete mole, retained in partial mole
★ Postevacuation **hCG plateau over 3 weeks or rise over 2 weeks** → evaluate GTN
Suspected neoplasia → chest imaging and stage/risk assessment; avoid biopsy of vascular vaginal metastasis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Stabilize bleeding → **suction curettage**; send tissue; give anti-D if Rh-negative
Hysterectomy an option when fertility not desired; surveillance remains necessary
Low-risk GTN → methotrexate or actinomycin D; high-risk → multiagent chemotherapy
hCG every 1–2 weeks until normal; partial: reconfirm after 1 month; complete: monthly for 6 months

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhage, thyroid storm, early hypertensive disease, invasive mole, metastatic malignancy
Chemotherapy toxicity; prognosis often excellent even with metastatic disease when treated

rows.label: Prevention
items: Reliable contraception during hCG surveillance; combined OCPs acceptable; defer pregnancy until follow-up complete
Future pregnancy → early ultrasound and postpregnancy hCG assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Multiple gestation: high hCG with recognizable normally developing fetuses
Missed abortion: nonviable gestation without trophoblastic overgrowth

table.title: Molar subtypes
rows: Usually triploid; maternal + two paternal sets

gestational-trophoblastic-disease.evidence: Surveillance checked 2026-10-30: [FIGO 2025 update](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12411817/); remaining pathology established teaching.

group-b-streptococcus-prophylaxis.name: Group B streptococcus prophylaxis
group-b-streptococcus-prophylaxis.scope: Universal rectovaginal screening (36-37 weeks), intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis indications (prior infant with GBS, bacteriuria, unknown status with fever, ROM >=18h, <37 weeks), IV penicillin G, penicillin allergy
group-b-streptococcus-prophylaxis.core: Intrapartum antibiotics reduce early-onset neonatal GBS disease in colonized patients and those with specified obstetric risk factors.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All pregnancies: culture; prior affected infant or current **GBS bacteriuria** → automatic prophylaxis

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Screen **36+0–37+6 weeks**; result generally valid 5 weeks
Begin antibiotics at labor or membrane rupture; aim ≥4 hours exposure without delaying delivery

rows.label: Test
items: **Rectovaginal culture**; request clindamycin susceptibility with serious penicillin allergy

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Positive culture → **IV penicillin G**; ampicillin acceptable
Unknown status + <37 weeks, temperature ≥38°C, or ROM ≥18 hours → prophylaxis
Suspected intra-amniotic infection → broad-spectrum antibiotics including GBS coverage

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Planned prelabor cesarean with **intact membranes** → no GBS prophylaxis, regardless of culture
GBS bacteriuria ≥100,000 CFU/mL or symptomatic UTI also needs antepartum treatment
Antepartum eradication of asymptomatic vaginal colonization does not replace intrapartum antibiotics

hyperglycemic-crises.name: Hyperglycemic crises
hyperglycemic-crises.core: Insulin-deficient diabetes with osmotic diuresis: rapid acidotic illness or slowly progressive hyperosmolar encephalopathy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Infection, missed insulin, pump failure, MI; DKA often type 1, HHS often older type 2
Euglycemic triggers: **SGLT2 inhibitors**, pregnancy, fasting

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, thirst, weight loss, dry mucosa, tachycardia
DKA: abdominal pain, vomiting, **Kussmaul (deep) breathing**; HHS: profound dehydration, focal deficits
★ Severe: **hypotension, stupor**, or coma → ICU

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin deficit + counterregulatory hormones → lipolysis, ketogenesis; residual insulin in HHS limits ketosis
Total-body K depleted despite initially normal/high serum K

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Glucose, electrolytes, venous pH, β-hydroxybutyrate**, osmolality; ECG + trigger evaluation
Effective osmolality = 2 × Na + glucose/18; glucose in mg/dL
★ HHS: **effective osmolality >300 OR total >320 mOsm/kg**; substantial ketosis/acidosis → mixed DKA/HHS
DKA resolution: ketones <0.6 mmol/L AND (pH ≥7.3 OR HCO₃ ≥18); urine ketones/anion gap misleading

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV isotonic crystalloid → K correction → IV regular insulin**; K <3.5 mmol/L → delay insulin
Replace K when <5 mmol/L; glucose checks every 1–2 h, electrolytes/pH/ketones every 4 h
★ Add **dextrose** below glucose 250; euglycemic presentation → immediately; continue insulin until crisis resolves
SC basal insulin overlaps infusion 1–2 h; bicarbonate only consider pH <7.0; HHS: slower osmolar correction

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, thrombosis; treatment: hypoglycemia, hypokalemic arrhythmias, cerebral edema (Cushing triad), hyperchloremic acidosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sick-day fluids/ketone checks; continue basal insulin; ensure supplies and early follow-up
Hold SGLT2 inhibitors during acute illness and before surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcoholic ketoacidosis: binge then poor intake; usually no diabetes
Starvation ketosis: usually milder acidosis, no marked hyperglycemia
Toxic alcohols: osmolar gap, exposure; absent substantial ketonemia

table.title: Biochemistry; ketones and HCO₃ in mmol/L

hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.name: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.scope: Chronic and gestational HTN, preeclampsia, HELLP, eclampsia
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.core: Pregnancy-associated hypertension; maternal organ injury or placental dysfunction signals danger even without substantial proteinuria.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior preeclampsia, chronic HTN, CKD, diabetes, SLE/APS, multifetal gestation
Nulliparity, obesity, age ≥35, family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Headache, visual disturbance, RUQ/epigastric pain, dyspnea; edema nonspecific
★ Severe features: **platelets <100,000/µL**, creatinine >1.1 mg/dL or doubled, transaminases ≥2× normal
Other severe features: pulmonary edema, refractory neurologic symptoms
Presentation through **6 weeks postpartum**; eclampsia/HELLP possible without prior HTN

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal spiral-artery remodeling → placental ischemia → systemic endothelial injury, vasospasm, capillary leak

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **BP ≥140/90**, either component, twice ≥4 h apart; severe ≥160/110 confirmed within minutes
CBC/platelets, creatinine, AST/ALT, urine protein; fetal growth US + antenatal testing
Proteinuria: **≥300 mg/24 h** or protein/creatinine ≥0.3; dipstick 2+ only if quantification unavailable
Chronic HTN + new proteinuria/end-organ injury → superimposed preeclampsia; HELLP: smear, LDH ≥600 IU/L

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Persistent severe BP ≥15 min → **IV labetalol/hydralazine** or immediate-release oral nifedipine within 30–60 min
★ Severe preeclampsia/eclampsia → **magnesium sulfate** through 24 h postpartum; airway before delivery
Chronic HTN ≥140/90 → oral labetalol/extended-release nifedipine; avoid ACE inhibitors/ARBs
Mg toxicity: areflexia/hypoventilation → stop infusion, **IV calcium gluconate**; oliguria → reduce dose

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, abruption, DIC, AKI, hepatic hematoma/rupture; fetal growth restriction, prematurity, death

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ High risk or multiple moderate risks → **aspirin 81 mg/day**, start 12–28 wk, ideally before 16
Postpartum BP review within 72 h if severe, otherwise 7–10 days; long-term cardiovascular follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: TTP: profound thrombocytopenia/hemolysis, persists after delivery
Acute fatty liver: hypoglycemia, jaundice, marked coagulopathy
Epilepsy: established seizure disorder; evaluate alternative causes despite obstetric context

table.title: Classification and delivery
rows: Before 20 wk or persists >12 wk postpartum
After 20 wk + proteinuria OR severe features
Severe BP alone sufficient; <34 stable → betamethasone
Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets
Deliver after stabilization, any gestational age

infertility.name: Infertility
infertility.scope: Definition (failure to conceive after 12 months), initial evaluation, semen analysis (male factor), ovulatory status (midluteal progesterone), tubal and uterine factors (hysterosalpingography), ovarian reserve testing
infertility.core: No conception after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; evaluate after 6 months at age ≥35, immediately over 40 or with risks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, PCOS, endometriosis, PID, pelvic surgery, chemotherapy, testicular injury, exogenous testosterone
Smoking, marked weight extremes, premature ovarian insufficiency, untreated endocrine disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/absent cycles → ovulatory dysfunction; galactorrhea → hyperprolactinemia; hot flashes → ovarian insufficiency
Prior ectopic pregnancy or chlamydia → tubal damage; normal cycles do not exclude male factor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failure of sperm production/delivery, oocyte release, fertilization, transport, or implantation; mixed factors common
Estrogen → proliferative endometrium; LH surge → ovulation
Corpus luteum **progesterone** → secretory endometrium, ↑basal body temperature

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Evaluate **both partners simultaneously**; reproductive history, sexual timing, examinations; semen analysis early
Abnormal semen result → repeat and male reproductive evaluation; do not begin with female laparoscopy
★ Ovulation uncertain → **progesterone about 7 days before expected menses**; >3 ng/mL supports ovulation
Regular 21–35-day cycles usually imply ovulation; targeted TSH, prolactin only for relevant symptoms
★ Ovulatory + normal semen → **HSG** (tubes) before laparoscopy; saline sonography: cavity; avoid in pregnancy/infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Anovulation/PCOS → **letrozole**, clomiphene alternative; hyperprolactinemia → cabergoline; correct thyroid disease
Tubal occlusion/severe male factor → IVF, sometimes intracytoplasmic sperm injection
Unexplained infertility → ovarian stimulation with intrauterine insemination, then IVF if unsuccessful
Intercourse every 1–2 days during fertile window; avoid testosterone for fertility-seeking men

rows.label: Complications
items: Psychological distress; stimulation → ovarian hyperstimulation, multiple gestation; assisted reproduction → ectopic pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: STI prevention, tobacco cessation, weight optimization; fertility preservation before gonadotoxic treatment
Preconception folic acid and medication review

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infrequent intercourse: inadequate exposure despite normal reproductive testing
Recurrent pregnancy loss: conception occurs, followed by repeated losses

table.title: Ovarian reserve: treatment response, not natural fertility
rows: Low values suggest reduced follicular pool

infertility.evidence: Evaluation checked 2026-10-30: [ASRM 2021](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/); treatment established reproductive guidance.

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate (own case), reason, communicate**; decision-specific, fluctuating
Competence: legal; diagnosis, age, alcohol use, incarceration, disagreement alone ≠ incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, even if life-saving or pregnant; avoid coercion, abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient
Refusing one therapy (blood) ≠ refusing all; provide other indicated care, including surgery

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no surrogate/directive/verified refusal → implied consent to treat
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or changed risk → renewed consent; consent revocable anytime before procedure

table.title: Who decides
rows: Ask whom to involve; facilitate promptly; no override
Minor decides; no parental consent (state law varies)
Parents seek unproven remedy for child
Continue proven therapy; investigate remedy; CPS not first
Close; discuss after waking; no next-of-kin consent
Autonomy ≠ entitlement; physician refuses, explains, offers alternatives

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

interstitial-cystitis.name: Interstitial cystitis
interstitial-cystitis.scope: Bladder pain syndrome, chronic pelvic pain relieved by voiding, urinary urgency and frequency, Hunner lesions on cystoscopy, dietary triggers, pentosan polysulfate, behavioral modification
interstitial-cystitis.core: Bladder-associated pain worsens with filling and improves after voiding, with urinary frequency but repeatedly negative infection testing.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: More common in women; associated chronic pelvic pain, fibromyalgia, IBS
Symptoms may flare with stress, intercourse, menstruation, acidic foods, caffeine, or alcohol

rows.label: Clues
items: Suprapubic pressure/discomfort, urgency, nocturia; often small voided volumes and dyspareunia
★ **Symptoms >6 weeks**, sterile cultures, no alternate explanation support bladder pain syndrome
Patients void to relieve discomfort rather than primarily to prevent urge incontinence
Fever, flank pain, gross hematuria, weight loss → evaluate other disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heterogeneous urothelial dysfunction, neural sensitization, and pelvic-floor muscle abnormalities generate chronic pain
Hunner-lesion subtype includes focal inflammatory mucosal injury; absence of lesions does not exclude disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **History, pelvic examination, urinalysis/culture**; review pain/voiding diary and check residual when retention suspected
Hematuria or cancer risk → malignancy evaluation rather than presumptive diagnosis
Cystoscopy when uncertain or suspect Hunner lesions; not required for every uncomplicated presentation
Glomerulations are nonspecific; potassium sensitivity testing is not recommended

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Education, trigger elimination, bladder training, stress management**; individualized multimodal treatment
Pelvic-floor tenderness → **manual physical therapy**; avoid strengthening/Kegel exercises when hypertonic
Persistent symptoms: selected amitriptyline, cimetidine, hydroxyzine, or intravesical lidocaine/heparin
★ **Pentosan polysulfate may cause pigmentary maculopathy**; discuss limited benefit and arrange retinal monitoring
Hunner lesions → cystoscopic fulguration or triamcinolone injection; refractory severe disease → specialist interventions

rows.label: Complications
items: Sleep disruption, sexual dysfunction, anxiety/depression, substantial quality-of-life impairment
Rare advanced fibrotic low-capacity bladder; treatments may cause sedation, anticholinergic effects, or retention

rows.label: Prevention
items: Identify individual dietary triggers; avoid unnecessary repeated antibiotics with negative cultures
Plan flare management and regular reassessment; no established primary-prevention strategy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Overactive bladder: urgency/incontinence predominates without filling-related pain
UTI: positive culture; bladder cancer: hematuria, risk factors, abnormal cystoscopy
Endometriosis: cyclic pelvic pain with gynecologic features

intra-amniotic-infection.name: Intra-amniotic infection
intra-amniotic-infection.scope: Chorioamnionitis, clinical diagnostic criteria (maternal fever, fetal tachycardia, purulent fluid, uterine tenderness), IV ampicillin and gentamicin, labor augmentation, postpartum endometritis
intra-amniotic-infection.core: Intrapartum fever with fetal tachycardia or purulent cervical drainage suggests ascending infection requiring antibiotics and delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prolonged membrane rupture, prolonged labor, repeated digital examinations after rupture, internal monitoring
Genital tract colonization; infection can occur with intact membranes

rows.label: Clues
items: Uterine tenderness, foul amniotic fluid, maternal tachycardia, leukocytosis
Hypotension, altered mentation, oliguria → maternal sepsis; leukocytosis alone nonspecific during labor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Polymicrobial ascent from vagina into decidua, membranes, amniotic fluid, and fetus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected infection: temperature **≥39°C**, or **38–38.9°C plus one additional clinical risk factor**
Additional factors: fetal baseline >160/min, purulent cervical drainage, maternal leukocytosis without corticosteroids
ACOG 2024 permits diagnosis without fever when other clinical findings strongly support infection
Clinical diagnosis; placental histology or amniotic-fluid testing confirms retrospectively; never delay treatment
Sepsis → blood cultures, lactate, CBC, renal function; cultures before antibiotics only without delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Prompt **IV ampicillin + gentamicin**, acetaminophen, IV fluids; notify neonatal team
★ Induce/augment labor with **oxytocin**; infection alone is not a cesarean indication
Cesarean for obstetric indication → add clindamycin for anaerobic coverage; postpartum dosing depends on course
Shock → fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine, urgent source control; do not await fetal lung maturity

rows.label: Complications
items: Uterine atony/hemorrhage, postpartum endometritis, bacteremia, septic shock
Neonatal pneumonia, sepsis, meningitis; prematurity-related morbidity
Endometritis: mixed aerobes/anaerobes; risks **cesarean** (strongest), prolonged rupture; shock → puerperal sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Minimize digital examinations after rupture; timely term-PROM induction; PPROM latency antibiotics when expectant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epidural-associated fever: sterile inflammation possible; cannot dismiss coexisting infection
★ Postpartum endometritis: fever, fundal tenderness → IV **clindamycin + gentamicin** first; older exams: ampicillin + gentamicin
Pyelonephritis: flank tenderness and positive urine culture

intra-amniotic-infection.evidence: Diagnostic update checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG 2024](https://doi.org/10.1097/aog.0000000000005593); management follows established ACOG teaching.

intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.name: Intrapartum fetal monitoring
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.scope: Baseline fetal heart rate, variability, early decelerations, late decelerations, variable decelerations, category I II III tracings, intrauterine resuscitation
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.core: Fetal oxygenation assessment from baseline, variability, and decelerations; persistent category III requires expedited delivery after immediate resuscitation.

rows.label: Definition
items: ★ Normal baseline **110–160/min**; moderate variability **6–25 beats/min**
Bradycardia <110; tachycardia >160; baseline change lasts ≥10 minutes
Tachysystole: >5 contractions/10 minutes over 30 minutes; oxytocin excess → late decelerations

rows.label: Interpret
items: Early: mirrors contraction → head compression; benign
Late: nadir after contraction peak → uteroplacental insufficiency
Variable: abrupt fall → cord compression; prolonged: 2–10 minutes

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Category II: lateral positioning, stop oxytocin, IV fluids; correct hypotension
Persistent tachysystole with concerning tracing → **terbutaline**; recurrent variables → amnioinfusion
★ Bradycardia: exam for cord prolapse; post-epidural → **maternal hypotension**; prepare delivery

rows.label: Compare
items: **Maternal fever** commonest tachycardia, variability kept; hypoxia → low variability, late decelerations
Transient minimal variability, no decelerations → **fetal sleep**, usually <40 minutes
Late decelerations → hypoxemia → **metabolic acidosis**; acute cord compression → respiratory acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Oxygen only for **maternal hypoxemia**; older routine-oxygen answers conflict with current guidance
Moderate variability or accelerations strongly argues against current metabolic acidemia
Category II alone does not mandate cesarean; reassess response and labor progress

table.title: Three-tier interpretation
rows: Reassuring rate/variability; no late or variable decelerations
Absent variability + recurrent late/variable decelerations or bradycardia
Resuscitate; unresolved → cesarean unless fully dilated
Evaluate severe anemia; expedite if persistent

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.name: Medical errors and patient safety
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.scope: Near miss, adverse event, error disclosure, root cause analysis, structured sign-outs and handoffs
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.core: Protect the patient first, disclose errors honestly, and redesign systems to reduce recurrence.

rows.label: Principle
items: Just culture: distinguish human error, risky shortcuts, and reckless conduct
Psychological safety enables reporting; accountability and system improvement can coexist
Effective communication: bedside verbal handoff with patient → real-time feedback, shared mental model

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Stabilize and mitigate harm**, notify supervising clinician, preserve relevant clinical information
★ Disclose facts, consequences, **apology**, treatment/prevention plans; update uncertainties
★ Report through institutional safety system; document clinical facts and disclosure in medical record

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid concealment, altered records, premature blame, or speculation about causation
Do not rely on education alone when workflow permits predictable repeated errors
Do not trust result delivery alone (fax, mail); **test-tracking log** verifies receipt, review, follow-up

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Reckless impairment/dangerous conduct → remove from unsafe duties; institutional escalation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Root cause analysis**: retrospective system investigation; identify multiple contributors
Failure mode and effects analysis: prospective hazard assessment before harm
Handoff: standardized I-PASS/SBAR, pending tasks, contingency plans, receiver synthesis/read-back

table.title: Event classification
rows: Unanticipated death/serious harm/life-saving rescue; prompts RCA
Upstream scheduling/staffing flaw; fix system, not individual

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.evidence: Not checked online; established patient-safety terminology and ethical disclosure principles.

multiple-gestation.name: Multiple gestation
multiple-gestation.scope: Dichorionic diamniotic (lambda sign), monochorionic diamniotic (T-sign), monochorionic monoamniotic, twin-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS), selective FGR, delivery timing recommendations
multiple-gestation.core: Chorionicity and amnionicity determine twin-specific surveillance, complications, and delivery timing; establish both on first-trimester ultrasound.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dizygotic twins: ovulation induction/assisted reproduction, maternal age, family history
Monozygotic splitting timing determines placental and sac sharing

rows.label: Clues
items: Uterus larger than dates, exaggerated pregnancy symptoms; ultrasound confirms fetal number
★ Shared placenta with **oligohydramnios/polyhydramnios sequence** → TTTS; small/absent donor bladder
Selective FGR: one small twin, discordant estimated weights; assess each umbilical artery Doppler

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental vascular anastomoses permit imbalanced flow in monochorionic twins
Donor hypovolemia reduces urine; recipient hypervolemia increases urine and cardiac strain

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **First-trimester ultrasound** identifies shared placenta and intertwin membrane
Monochorionic diamniotic → ultrasound **every 2 weeks from 16 weeks** for fluid/bladders
Serial growth in all twins; Doppler and more frequent assessment when growth discordance develops
TTTS donor deepest pocket ≤2 cm, recipient ≥8 cm; staging incorporates bladder, Doppler, hydrops

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ TTTS stages II–IV at 16–26 weeks → **fetoscopic laser ablation** of placental anastomoses
Asymptomatic stage I → at least weekly surveillance; refer fetal intervention center if progression/symptoms
★ Diamniotic twins with **first twin cephalic** may deliver vaginally with experienced team
Monoamniotic twins → cesarean; fetal deterioration, preeclampsia, or severe growth issues may require earlier delivery

rows.label: Complications
items: Preterm birth, preeclampsia, anemia, gestational diabetes, postpartum hemorrhage
Monoamniotic cord entanglement; monochorionic co-twin death can cause surviving twin neurologic injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia prevention; optimize iron/nutrition; single-embryo transfer reduces iatrogenic multiples

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates/macrosomia: enlarged uterus but singleton on imaging
Twin anemia-polycythemia sequence: discordant MCA velocities without major fluid imbalance

ovarian-torsion.name: Ovarian torsion
ovarian-torsion.scope: Ovarian cyst, ovarian torsion, Doppler ultrasonography, detorsion, cystectomy
ovarian-torsion.core: Abrupt unilateral pelvic pain with nausea and vomiting suggests twisting of the adnexal vascular pedicle, requiring rapid ovarian-preserving surgical assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Ovarian cyst/mass, especially >5 cm; pregnancy, ovulation induction, prior torsion
Functional cysts and mature teratomas common lead points; adolescents may torsion a normal ovary

rows.label: Clues
items: Intermittent severe pain from twisting/untwisting; adnexal tenderness or mass; mild leukocytosis possible
Fever, guarding, peritoneal findings may indicate advanced ischemia; absence does not reassure
Pregnancy test can be positive with torsion; pregnancy does not establish ectopic implantation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Venous/lymphatic outflow obstruction → congestion and edema, followed by reduced arterial inflow
Dual arterial supply may preserve detectable flow despite clinically important vascular compromise

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; assess shock, competing surgical diagnoses
★ **Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler** first; transvaginal when feasible, transabdominal in younger adolescents
Enlarged edematous ovary, peripheral follicles, free fluid, twisted pedicle support diagnosis
★ **Normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion**; no laboratory test reliably rules it out
High clinical suspicion → diagnostic laparoscopy; no serial imaging delay to prove loss of flow

rows.label: Tx
items: NPO, IV access, fluids for dehydration, analgesia/antiemetic; urgent gynecology consultation
★ **Laparoscopic detorsion with ovarian preservation**, even if dark/blue appearance
Cystectomy if safely feasible; friable edematous ovary → defer cyst removal and reassess
Oophorectomy only if unavoidable tissue destruction or compelling malignancy concern; avoid removal for color alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Ovarian infarction, diminished ovarian reserve, infertility, recurrent torsion
Unnecessary extensive resection sacrifices viable ovarian tissue; timely treatment maximizes salvage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Residual cyst → **ultrasound at 6–12 weeks**; persistent significant cyst may need elective cystectomy
Ovulation suppression may reduce recurrent functional cysts; oophoropexy individualized after recurrent torsion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine gestation or concerning pregnancy-location evaluation
Ruptured hemorrhagic cyst: abrupt pain with free fluid; often improves without persistent torsion signs
PID: discharge, cervical motion tenderness, STI risk; bilateral symptoms more typical

palliative-and-hospice-care.name: Palliative and hospice care
palliative-and-hospice-care.scope: Hospice eligibility, pain control, goals of care, surrogate requests
palliative-and-hospice-care.core: Palliative care relieves suffering at any illness stage; hospice centers care on comfort when prognosis and patient goals support a terminal-care benefit.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ **Patient goals and informed consent** guide intervention burdens; symptom relief remains an obligation
Proportionate opioids for pain/dyspnea permissible despite risks; reassess sedation/respiration
Codeine fails → morphine/oxycodone; pain mimics depression; wears off early → shorten interval

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Ask understanding/values → discuss prognosis → recommend a goal-concordant plan
Assess capacity; use advance directive, then authorized surrogate: substituted judgment/best interests
★ Titrate **opioids**, short-acting for breakthrough; constipation → keep dose, add stimulant laxative

rows.label: Don't
items: DNR ≠ no antibiotics, fluids, nutrition or other desired treatment
Capable patient’s informed wishes override surrogate requests
No nonbeneficial interventions; explain reasoning, offer alternatives, seek ethics review for conflict

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Refractory terminal suffering → proportional palliative sedation, specialist review and consent
Emergency, unknown preferences → stabilize while clarifying wishes; honor documented refusals
Advanced dementia refusing intake → comfort hand-feeding by mouth; no tubes or IV

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Hospice: **≤6-month prognosis** if usual course; longer survival permits recertification
Hospice: unrelated conditions remain treatable; no DNR requirement; enrollment revocable if goals change
Cancer pain: escalating requests → tolerance/progression, not addiction; past OUD never limits analgesia

palliative-and-hospice-care.evidence: Eligibility checked 2026-10-30: [CMS hospice benefit](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-for-service-providers/hospice); clinical ethics: established teaching.

table.title: Care settings
rows: Adjust with hospice team; avoid readmission

placenta-accreta-spectrum.name: Placenta accreta spectrum
placenta-accreta-spectrum.scope: Placenta accreta, placenta increta, placenta percreta, prior cesarean and placenta previa risk, antenatal ultrasound diagnosis, scheduled cesarean hysterectomy
placenta-accreta-spectrum.core: Abnormal placental invasion into myometrium after prior uterine surgery, causing catastrophic postpartum hemorrhage if manual removal is attempted.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Prior cesarean delivery + placenta previa** (strongest risk; rises with each cesarean)
Prior myomectomy, dilation and curettage, Asherman syndrome, advanced maternal age

rows.label: Clues
items: Often **asymptomatic** until delivery; painless third-trimester bleeding if previa coexists
★ **Placenta fails to detach** after delivery with brisk bleeding on traction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective **decidua basalis** at scar site lets chorionic villi attach directly to myometrium

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Antenatal ultrasound with Doppler**: placental lacunae, lost retroplacental clear zone
**Pelvic MRI** when ultrasound is inconclusive or posterior/percreta invasion is suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Scheduled cesarean hysterectomy at 34–35+6 wk** at tertiary center; **leave placenta in situ**
★ **Never attempt manual placental removal** → triggers massive hemorrhage
Massive transfusion protocol ready; antenatal betamethasone if delivering <37 wk
IF found unexpectedly during delivery → stop traction, close hysterotomy, perform hysterectomy

rows.label: Complications
items: **Massive postpartum hemorrhage**, DIC, hysterectomy/infertility, bladder or ureteral injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary primary cesarean deliveries; screen all placenta previa patients with targeted ultrasound

rows.label: Mimics
items: Retained placenta: normal cleavage plane present; detaches with manual extraction
Uterine atony: boggy uterus after complete placental delivery; responds to uterotonics
Placenta previa alone: painless bleeding, but normal retroplacental clear zone on ultrasound

placenta-accreta-spectrum.evidence: Not checked online; established ACOG/SMFM teaching.

postpartum-care.name: Postpartum care
postpartum-care.scope: Normal puerperal changes, lochia, uterine involution, perineal and cesarean wound healing, breastfeeding, postpartum depression screening, routine postpartum visit
postpartum-care.core: Postpartum care is an ongoing assessment of recovery, mood, infant feeding, contraception, and chronic disease after every birth.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All postpartum patients; assess support, sleep, safety, sexual health, and reproductive goals

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Contact within **3 weeks**; comprehensive visit by **12 weeks**, with earlier risk-based review
Hypertensive disorder → BP within 7–10 days; severe hypertension → within 72 hours

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Edinburgh or PHQ-9 depression screen; assess suicidality directly after positive self-harm response
BP, bleeding, fundal tenderness; inspect perineum/incision for erythema, drainage, separation
Observe latch/milk transfer; frequent feeds, lactation support; cracked nipples → correct positioning

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Heavy bleeding (pad soaked <1 hour), fever, dyspnea, severe headache → urgent evaluation
Mood screen positive → diagnostic interview, psychotherapy/SSRI; psychosis → emergency hospitalization
Increasing wound pain/purulence → evaluate infection; breast fluctuance → ultrasound for abscess

rows.label: Traps
items: Ovulation may precede first period; discuss contraception before discharge
Lactational contraception: amenorrhea, exclusive frequent breastfeeding, infant <6 months
Postpartum hypertension and cardiomyopathy can first appear after discharge

table.title: Expected recovery
rows: Red rubra → pink serosa → white/yellow alba
Descends daily; near prepregnancy size by 6 weeks
Pain improves; pulling normal if intact; keep clean
Early cramping and fluid loss; breastfeeding intensifies cramping

postpartum-care.evidence: Visit timing checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG postpartum care](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/05/optimizing-postpartum-care); normal physiology established teaching.

recurrent-pregnancy-loss.name: Recurrent pregnancy loss
recurrent-pregnancy-loss.scope: Definition (two or more losses), antiphospholipid syndrome, congenital uterine anomalies (septate, bicornuate), parental chromosomal translocations, endocrine causes, diagnostic workup
recurrent-pregnancy-loss.core: Two or more spontaneous pregnancy losses warrant evaluation; ASRM 2026 includes hCG-confirmed biochemical losses and excludes confirmed ectopic or molar pregnancies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal age/aneuploidy, parental rearrangements, APS, uterine anomalies, uncontrolled diabetes/hypothyroidism
Smoking, obesity; many recurrent losses remain unexplained despite evaluation

rows.label: Clues
items: Repeated early loss favors chromosomal causes; later loss may suggest anatomy or placental disease
Prior thrombosis, fetal death ≥10 weeks, or early severe preeclampsia raises APS suspicion
Painless second-trimester dilation suggests cervical insufficiency rather than a primary endocrine cause
Unilateral renal agenesis + recurrent loss → **Müllerian uterine anomaly**, not APS

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryonic genetic imbalance, abnormal uterine cavity, or placental thromboinflammation disrupts successful gestation
Septum has abnormal implantation environment; balanced carriers can produce unbalanced embryos

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Miscarriage-tissue chromosomal microarray** when feasible; result guides further evaluation
★ **Uterine cavity assessment**: saline sonography, HSG, or hysteroscopy; 3D ultrasound distinguishes external contour
Parental karyotypes if unbalanced rearrangement found or tissue testing unavailable; offer genetic counseling
APS clinical criteria → lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-β2-glycoprotein I; repeat positives ≥12 weeks later
TSH for symptoms/risk or unexplained/euploid losses; HbA1c with diabetes risks; prolactin only with suggestive symptoms

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Confirmed obstetric APS → **aspirin + heparin**; treat overt thyroid disease and uncontrolled diabetes
Septum/cavity lesion → discuss hysteroscopic correction; live-birth benefit uncertain
Translocation → reproductive genetic counseling, expectant conception or IVF with targeted genetic testing
★ Unexplained loss → support and expectant care; **no empiric anticoagulation**
Vaginal progesterone may be offered with early bleeding/prior recurrent loss after discussing uncertain benefit

rows.label: Complications
items: Grief, anxiety/depression; repeated uterine instrumentation → adhesions; treatment burden and financial stress

rows.label: Prevention
items: Preconception folic acid, smoking cessation, metabolic optimization; early supportive follow-up in next pregnancy
Avoid routine inherited thrombophilia, NK-cell, infectious panels, or ovarian-reserve tests without separate indications

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infertility: failure to achieve pregnancy rather than loss after conception
Sporadic miscarriage: common isolated aneuploid event, no recurrent-loss workup after one uncomplicated loss

recurrent-pregnancy-loss.evidence: Updated workup checked 2026-10-30: [ASRM 2026](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/recurrent-pregnancy-loss-a-committee-opinion-2026/); anatomy established teaching.

routine-prenatal-care.name: Routine prenatal care and early pregnancy
routine-prenatal-care.scope: Pregnancy diagnosis (beta-hCG), initial prenatal assessment, routine first-trimester screening, aneuploidy screening
routine-prenatal-care.core: Confirm and date pregnancy, assess maternal risks, offer one aneuploidy-screening strategy or diagnostic testing, and arrange time-sensitive prenatal studies.

rows.label: Who
items: All pregnancies; review obstetric history, drugs, illness, substance use, violence, family history
Offer carrier screening and genetic counseling; discuss patient preferences and right to decline

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Early visit: urine hCG confirms pregnancy; serum quantitative hCG for uncertain/complicated cases
★ First-trimester **ultrasound crown–rump length** best establishes gestational age
Serum screen 10–13 6/7 weeks; NT 11–13 6/7; cfDNA from 10 weeks

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Initial **CBC, ABO/Rh, antibody screen, urine culture**; HIV, syphilis, HBsAg, HCV, rubella immunity
GC/chlamydia by age/risk; offer one aneuploidy strategy regardless of maternal age
Anatomy ultrasound 18–22 weeks; AFP for open neural tube defects when not otherwise assessed

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Abnormal screen → counseling, ultrasound, **CVS/amniocentesis** before irreversible decisions
CVS: 10–13 weeks; amniocentesis: ≥15 weeks; neither automatically required after negative screening
Rh-negative, unsensitized → anti-D prophylaxis at 28 weeks and after sensitizing events

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **cfDNA is screening**, not diagnostic; does not screen open neural tube defects
Single hCG value cannot establish viability or location; pain/bleeding → ectopic evaluation
Folate before conception/early gestation; avoid alcohol, tobacco, teratogens; no live vaccines

table.title: Early and routine pregnancy calls
rows: Nausea, irregular bleeding or amenorrhea, even premenarche
Missed menses, urinary frequency, friable cervix, enlarged uterus
Brief sharp movement-triggered lower-quadrant pain, normal vitals
No added preterm, fluid, or placental risk

type-1-diabetes-mellitus.name: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
type-1-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Autoimmune islet destruction, honeymoon phase, diabetic nephropathy screening, microalbuminuria, intensive insulin
type-1-diabetes-mellitus.core: Autoimmune beta-cell destruction causing absolute insulin deficiency; onset at any age, sometimes initially mistaken for type 2 diabetes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childhood/adolescent onset common but any age possible; family history, HLA-associated autoimmune susceptibility
Associated autoimmune thyroid disease and celiac disease; immune checkpoint inhibitors can cause insulin-deficient diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, polydipsia, nocturia, weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision
★ **Vomiting, abdominal pain, Kussmaul breathing, dehydration** → evaluate DKA immediately
Honeymoon: temporary partial beta-cell recovery after diagnosis → lower insulin requirement, not cure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: T-cell-mediated islet destruction → impaired peripheral glucose uptake, hepatic glucose output and lipolysis/ketogenesis
Absent endogenous insulin → low C-peptide; glycemic variability worsened by inconsistent carbohydrate intake/exercise

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Symptoms + **random glucose ≥200 mg/dL**; otherwise A1c ≥6.5%, fasting ≥126, or 2-hour OGTT ≥200
Without unequivocal hyperglycemia/crisis → confirm with second abnormal result; never delay insulin in suspected DKA
GAD65, IA-2 or ZnT8 antibodies help classify uncertain cases; antibody negativity does not exclude
★ Adults: annual **urine albumin/creatinine ratio + eGFR after 5 years**; eye examination within 5 years
Albuminuria ≥30 mg/g: confirm 2 of 3 samples over 3–6 months; exclude exercise/infection-related elevations

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Basal-bolus insulin or pump + CGM**; carbohydrate-based mealtime dosing; automated delivery preferred when feasible
DKA → isotonic fluids, potassium-guided replacement, IV insulin after excluding severe hypokalemia
Typical adult A1c goal <7%, individualized for hypoglycemia/comorbidity
Hypoglycemia awake → rapid oral glucose; impaired consciousness → glucagon or IV dextrose
Hypertension + albuminuria → ACE inhibitor/ARB; no preventive RAAS blockade with normal BP/UACR/eGFR

rows.label: Complications
items: DKA, treatment-associated hypoglycemia; retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, accelerated atherosclerosis
Repeated injections into same site → lipohypertrophy and erratic absorption
Periconception hyperglycemia → **congenital heart defects** most common anomaly

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Never omit basal insulin**; sick-day glucose/ketone checks, hydration, rescue glucagon and medical identification
Foot care, BP/lipid control, vaccination; TSH; celiac serology soon after diagnosis or with symptoms
Preconception: **tight glycemic control, A1c <6.5%** → fewer anomalies, pregnancy loss; folate alone insufficient

rows.label: Mimics
items: Type 2 diabetes: insulin resistance, usually preserved C-peptide; obesity does not exclude type 1
MODY: multigenerational young-onset diabetes, negative antibodies, preserved endogenous insulin
Diabetes insipidus: polyuria with dilute urine, normal glucose, often hypernatremia

type-1-diabetes-mellitus.evidence: Screening/diagnosis checked 2026-10-30: [ADA CKD Standards, 2026](https://doi.org/10.2337/dc26-s011); [ADA diagnosis Standards, 2026](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S27/163926); other care: established diabetes teaching.

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery/radiation suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stress: aging/multiparity weaken pelvic floor → **urethral hypermobility**, low sphincter tone
Urge: **uninhibited detrusor contractions** (detrusor instability), worsened by caffeine; MS lesion → low residual
Overflow: **detrusor underactivity/acontractile bladder** (MS, diabetes, stroke) or outlet obstruction → high residual
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
**Q-tip excursion >30°** on Valsalva → urethral hypermobility (urethrocele)
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic (oxybutynin); discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

vaginitis.name: Vaginitis
vaginitis.scope: Bacterial vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Vulvovaginal candidiasis, atrophic vaginitis, genitourinary syndrome of menopause
vaginitis.core: Vaginal discharge or irritation requires distinction among dysbiosis, sexually transmitted protozoal infection, yeast overgrowth, and hypoestrogenic mucosal change.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: BV: new partners, douching; trichomoniasis: sexual exposure
Candida: antibiotics, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression; atrophy: menopause or other hypoestrogenic states
Prepubertal: hand inoculation of respiratory pathogens during URI

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus, dysuria, dyspareunia; discharge appearance overlaps, so symptoms alone insufficient
★ **Fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness** → evaluate PID rather than isolated vaginitis
Postmenopausal bleeding needs assessment beyond assuming atrophy
★ Prepubertal **foul purulent/bloody discharge** → retained vaginal **foreign body**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: BV: lactobacilli depleted, anaerobes expand; Candida causes inflammatory overgrowth
Low estrogen thins epithelium and reduces lactobacilli → mucosal fragility and elevated vaginal pH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Vaginal pH, saline/KOH microscopy**, history and examination; NAAT improves infectious diagnosis
BV: ≥3 Amsel—discharge, ↑pH, clue cells, amine odor; Gardnerella culture unhelpful (normal flora)
★ Suspected trichomoniasis + negative wet mount → **NAAT**, not reassurance
Recurrent/complicated Candida → culture or PCR for species; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **oral metronidazole 7 days in women**; treat partners, abstain until completed/resolved
BV → oral metronidazole 7 days or vaginal metronidazole/clindamycin, **no routine partner treatment**, ACOG: treat if recurrent; treat symptomatic pregnancy
Candida → topical azole/nystatin or oral fluconazole; **pregnancy: topical azole 7 days**, avoid oral fluconazole
GSM → moisturizers/lubricants, then low-dose vaginal estrogen for persistent symptoms
Recurrent BV: ACOG 2025 considers male-partner metronidazole + topical clindamycin; older boards omit

rows.label: Complications
items: BV/trichomoniasis associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and increased STI acquisition
Recurrent symptoms → reassess diagnosis, adherence, reinfection, diabetes or resistant/non-albicans yeast

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **retest women at about 3 months**; condoms
Avoid douching/irritants; no routine partner treatment for uncomplicated Candida

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: endocervical mucopus, friability, positive GC/CT NAAT
Contact dermatitis: external irritation after product exposure
Sarcoma botryoides: girl with bleeding, grape-like polypoid vaginal mass

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, inherited thrombophilia
**Previous VTE** is the strongest predictor of recurrence; remote surgery months ago adds little
**Central venous catheter** → main cause of upper-extremity DVT

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload
Massive PE: high RA/PA pressure, low PCWP, low output; RV infarct: PA pressure normal/low

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week
Low-probability V/Q + high clinical suspicion is nondiagnostic → **CT angiography**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; cancer → LMWH/DOAC; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible
Acute proximal DVT/PE without DOAC → immediate **heparin**; warfarin alone never initial; inferior in cancer

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Aspirin or 1 month inadequate; DOACs now preferred, older exam questions may expect warfarin 3–6 months
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization
Hip arthroplasty → LMWH, warfarin or DOAC; aspirin now accepted, older exam questions may expect anticoagulant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome
Amniotic fluid embolism: peripartum collapse with **DIC/low fibrinogen**
